SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is child labour? (1 mark)
   A. Light help at home
   B. Playing sports
   C. Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   D. Doing homework

2. What should you do if someone makes you feel unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   B. Fight
   C. Stay silent
   D. Keep it a secret

3. Which day is celebrated on 16 June each year to honour children in Africa? (1 mark)
   A. Madaraka Day
   B. Day of the African Child
   C. Labour Day
   D. Jamhuri Day

4. Which action helps a child with special needs? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at them
   B. Hiding them
   C. Including them in games
   D. Neglecting them

5. What is a right? (1 mark)
   A. Something every person is allowed to have or do
   B. A game
   C. A punishment
   D. A chore

6. What is an election? (1 mark)
   A. A process where people vote to choose leaders
   B. A kind of game
   C. A school holiday
   D. A prayer

7. What is a ballot paper? (1 mark)
   A. A menu
   B. A paper on which a voter marks a choice
   C. A ticket for a bus
   D. A kind of book

8. What does equality mean in an election? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers vote
   B. Each person has one vote of equal value
   C. Only boys vote
   D. Some people have many votes

9. What is an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   B. A kind of food
   C. A sports match
   D. A game

10. Which is a function of the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   B. Beating pupils
   C. Setting exams
   D. Collecting fees

11. What should a Children's Government NOT do? (1 mark)
   A. Represent pupils
   B. Punish other pupils by itself
   C. Welcome visitors
   D. Organise clean-up days

12. Why is a Children's Government important? (1 mark)
   A. It punishes children
   B. It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility
   C. It stops learning
   D. It closes the school

13. What does a patron do? (1 mark)
   A. Drives the bus
   B. Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   C. Wins all elections
   D. Cooks for pupils

14. Why is it important for leaders to have good qualities? (1 mark)
   A. People quarrel
   B. People fear them
   C. Resources are wasted
   D. People trust them and live in peace

15. Which activity can show leadership qualities in class? (1 mark)
   A. Copying
   B. Sleeping
   C. Fighting
   D. Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel

16. Who leads a sub-location? (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. President
   C. Governor
   D. Assistant chief

17. What are ECDE and pre-primary schools run by? (1 mark)
   A. The army
   B. County governments
   C. Foreign governments
   D. Private banks only

18. Who is the head of the national government? (1 mark)
   A. The Governor
   B. The MCA
   C. The President
   D. The Speaker

19. Which best describes the difference between the governor and an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. They do the same job
   B. The governor makes laws
   C. An MCA is above the governor
   D. The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor

20. What does the county assembly do? (1 mark)
   A. Cooks meals
   B. Drives buses
   C. Trains footballers
   D. Makes county laws and approves the budget

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe the steps in a fair class election. (4 marks)

22. Explain how citizens can support the county government. (4 marks)

23. Explain why it is important to have a Children's Government in school. (4 marks)

24. Explain why children with special needs need extra care and respect. (3 marks)

25. Name the two main parts of a county government and state what each does. (4 marks)

26. Explain the difference between a chief and a clan elder. (3 marks)

27. Explain what may happen in a community with dishonest leaders. (3 marks)

28. Explain how a class representative helps classmates. (3 marks)

29. Give two responsibilities of a child at school. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   Child labour is harmful and illegal.

2. A — Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   Telling an adult is right.

3. B — Day of the African Child
   16 June is the Day of the African Child.

4. C — Including them in games
   Children with special needs have equal rights.

5. A — Something every person is allowed to have or do
   Rights protect people.

6. A — A process where people vote to choose leaders
   Elections choose leaders.

7. B — A paper on which a voter marks a choice
   Voters mark ballot papers.

8. B — Each person has one vote of equal value
   Everyone's vote counts the same.

9. A — A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   An agenda gives the order of business.

10. A — Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   Leaders help with order and cleanliness.

11. B — Punish other pupils by itself
   Only teachers decide on discipline.

12. B — It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility
   It teaches leadership and democracy.

13. B — Guides and advises the pupil leaders
   The patron is a teacher adviser.

14. D — People trust them and live in peace
   Good leaders build trust and peace.

15. D — Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
   Role play shows how leaders act.

16. D — Assistant chief
   An assistant chief leads a sub-location.

17. B — County governments
   Pre-primary education is a county function.

18. C — The President
   The President leads the national government.

19. D — The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor
   They have different roles.

20. D — Makes county laws and approves the budget
   The assembly makes laws and approves the budget.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Announce, nominate candidates, campaign, vote, count votes in public, and declare the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group of two correct steps.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Attend public meetings, vote, pay fees and taxes, and take care of public property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: It gives pupils a voice, teaches leadership, helps teachers with order and cleanliness, and teaches democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: They have the same rights as other children. They may be laughed at or neglected. Including them helps them to learn and be happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: The county executive runs the county and carries out laws. The county assembly makes county laws and checks the executive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part and 1 mark for each job.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: A chief is appointed by the national government to lead a location. A clan elder is respected by a clan for age and wisdom and keeps customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Resources are wasted, people lose trust, and people quarrel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: They bring classmates' ideas and complaints to meetings, tell the class what was decided, and help solve small problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attend and study hard, and respect others. Accept care for property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each responsibility.
